title: Diosgenin Alleviates Age-Related Sarcopenia by Promoting Satellite Cell Proliferation and Myogenic Differentiation via Activation of the SIRT1/PGC-1alpha Signaling Pathway.
authors: Zeng, Xin; Ding, Han; Li, Ziye; Wang, Qian; Guan, Peiyao; Wang, Tingting; Wang, Jiayun; Fu, Yansong; Chen, Lizhang; Qin, Hong
one_liner_zh: 该文研究薯蓣皂苷通过SIRT1/PGC-1alpha通路改善老年性肌少症，核心是药物-蛋白互作与肌肉细胞分化，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Age-related sarcopenia is characterized by a progressive decline in skeletal muscle mass and function, with satellite cell dysfunction representing a central pathogenic mechanism. Diosgenin, a steroidal saponin derived from plants of the Dioscorea genus, has demonstrated potential anti-aging properties; however, its role in sarcopenia remains unclear. In this study, naturally aged C57BL/6J mice and a D-galactose (D-gal)-induced senescent C2C12 cell model were employed to systematically investigate the effects of diosgenin on muscle function, satellite cell dynamics, and the sirtuin 1 (SIRT1)/peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator-1 alpha (PGC-1alpha) signaling pathway. Diosgenin treatment significantly improved forelimb grip strength and exercise endurance, increased the gastrocnemius muscle index, and enlarged muscle fiber cross-sectional area in aged mice. Mechanistically, diosgenin upregulated the expression of myokines meteorin-like protein (METRNL) and insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) at both mRNA and protein levels, increased the number of proliferative satellite cells positive for paired box 7 (Pax7) and Ki67, and enhanced the expression of myogenic markers, including myogenic factor 5 (Myf5), Pax7, and myosin heavy chain II (MyHC II). These effects were mediated by direct activation of SIRT1, leading to deacetylation of PGC-1alpha. Notably, pharmacological inhibition of SIRT1 with EX527 markedly abrogated the diosgenin-induced effects. Molecular docking and cellular thermal shift assays further confirmed the direct interaction between diosgenin and SIRT1. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that diosgenin alleviates age-related sarcopenia by activating the SIRT1/PGC-1alpha signaling pathway to promote satellite cell proliferation and myogenic differentiation, highlighting its potential as a promising therapeutic candidate for sarcopenia.
abstract_zh: 年龄相关性肌少症（sarcopenia）以骨骼肌质量和功能的进行性下降为特征，其中卫星细胞功能障碍是核心致病机制之一。薯蓣皂苷元（diosgenin）是一种来源于薯蓣属（Dioscorea）植物的甾体皂苷，已显示出潜在的抗衰老特性；然而，其在肌少症中的作用尚不明确。本研究采用自然衰老的C57BL/6J小鼠和D-半乳糖（D-gal）诱导的衰老C2C12细胞模型，系统探讨了薯蓣皂苷元对肌肉功能、卫星细胞动态变化以及去乙酰化酶1（SIRT1）/过氧化物酶体增殖物激活受体γ共激活因子1α（PGC-1alpha）信号通路的影响。薯蓣皂苷元处理显著改善了老年小鼠的前肢握力和运动耐力，增加了腓肠肌指数，并扩大了肌纤维横截面积。在机制上，薯蓣皂苷元在mRNA和蛋白水平上调了肌因子meteorin样蛋白（METRNL）和胰岛素样生长因子1（IGF-1）的表达，增加了表达配对盒7（Pax7）和Ki67的增殖性卫星细胞数量，并增强了成肌标志物（包括成肌因子5（Myf5）、Pax7和肌球蛋白重链II（MyHC II））的表达。这些效应通过直接激活SIRT1介导，导致PGC-1alpha去乙酰化。值得注意的是，使用EX527药理学抑制SIRT1可显著消除薯蓣皂苷元诱导的效应。分子对接和细胞热位移实验进一步证实了薯蓣皂苷元与SIRT1之间的直接相互作用。综上所述，这些发现表明，薯蓣皂苷元通过激活SIRT1/PGC-1alpha信号通路促进卫星细胞增殖和成肌分化，从而缓解年龄相关性肌少症，凸显其作为肌少症潜在治疗候选药物的前景。
